44	/**
45	 * The base class for inference manager. An inference manager is a wrapper
46	 * around the output channel and the official equality engine of a Theory.
47	 * It is used for ensuring that the equality engine and output channel
48	 * are used properly. This includes the following invariants:
49	 *
50	 * (1) The state tracks conflicts.
51	 * In particular, TheoryState::isInConflict returns true whenever we have
52	 * called OutputChannel::conflict in the current context, which we enforce
53	 * by always setting d_state.notifyInConflict at the same time we send
54	 * conflicts on the output channel.
55	 *
56	 * (2) The theory is notified of (internal) facts.
57	 * In particular, Theory::preNotifyFact and Theory::notifyFact are called
58	 * (with isInternal = true) whenever we assert internal facts using
59	 * assertFactInernal below, mirroring what is done for facts from the fact
60	 * queue (where isInternal = false).
61	 *
62	 * (3) The proof equality engine is used whenever proofs are enabled (when
63	 * the proof node manager provided to this class is non-null). Notice this
64	 * class automatically will construct a proof equality engine during
65	 * setEqualityEngine, and use it for handling variants of assertInternalFact
66	 * below that involve proofs.
67	 */
68	class TheoryInferenceManager : protected EnvObj
69	{
70	  typedef context::CDHashSet<Node> NodeSet;
71	
72	 public:

78	   * @param pnm The proof node manager, which if non-null, enables proofs for
79	   * this inference manager
80	   * @param statsName The name of the inference manager, which is used for
81	   * giving unique names for statistics,

84	   * only lemmas that are unique after rewriting are sent to the theory engine
85	   * from this inference manager.
86	   */

88	                         Theory& t,
89	                         TheoryState& state,
90	                         const std::string& statsName,
91	                         bool cacheLemmas = true);
92	  virtual ~TheoryInferenceManager();
93	  //--------------------------------------- initialization
94	  /**
95	   * Set equality engine, ee is a pointer to the official equality engine
96	   * of theory.
97	   */
98	  void setEqualityEngine(eq::EqualityEngine* ee);
99	  /** Set the decision manager */

101	  //--------------------------------------- end initialization
102	  /**
103	   * Are proofs enabled in this inference manager? Returns true if the proof
104	   * node manager pnm provided to the constructor of this class was non-null.
105	   */
106	  bool isProofEnabled() const;
107	  /** Get the underlying proof equality engine */
108	  eq::ProofEqEngine* getProofEqEngine();
109	  /**
110	   * Reset, which resets counters regarding the number of added lemmas and
111	   * internal facts. This method should be manually called by the theory at
112	   * the appropriate time for the purpose of tracking the usage of this
113	   * inference manager.
114	   *
115	   * For example, some theories implement an internal checking loop that
116	   * repeats while new facts are added. The theory should call reset at the
117	   * beginning of this loop and repeat its strategy while hasAddedFact is true.
118	   */

123	   */
124	  bool hasSent() const;

140	   */

143	  /**
144	   * Raise conflict, called when constants a and b merge. Sends the conflict

150	   * EqualityEngineNotify::eqNotifyConstantTermMerge.
151	   */

213	   */

216	   * Explained lemma. This should be called when

239	                ProofRule pfr,
240	                const std::vector<Node>& exp,
241	                const std::vector<Node>& noExplain,
242	                const std::vector<Node>& args,
243	                LemmaProperty p = LemmaProperty::NONE);
244	  /**
245	   * Make the trust node for the above method. It is responsibility of the
246	   * caller to subsequently call trustedLemma with the returned trust node.
247	   */
248	  TrustNode mkLemmaExp(Node conc,
249	                       ProofRule id,
250	                       const std::vector<Node>& exp,
251	                       const std::vector<Node>& noExplain,
252	                       const std::vector<Node>& args);
253	  /**
254	   * Same as above, but where pg can provide a proof of conc from free
255	   * assumptions in exp. This sends a trusted lemma on the output channel where
256	   * the proof equality engine is the proof generator. The generator pg
257	   * is asked to provide the final step(s) of this proof during this call.
258	   *
259	   * @param conc The conclusion of the lemma
260	   * @param exp The set of (all) literals that imply conc

266	   */

268	                InferenceId id,
269	                const std::vector<Node>& exp,

276	   */

278	                       const std::vector<Node>& exp,
279	                       const std::vector<Node>& noExplain,

facts: Q1: preferPhase exists; requirePhase does NOT exist as any callable API. The only occurrences of 'requirePhase' in src/ are a local out-parameter bool in TheoryProxy::getNextDecisionRequest (src/prop/theory_proxy.cpp:380) and its CaDiCaL consumer (src/prop/cadical/cdclt_propagator.cpp:220-310), which belong to the decision-strategy path, not the phase API.

Q1: TheoryInferenceManager::preferPhase(TNode n, bool pol) is declared at src/theory/theory_inference_manager.h:359 and defined at src/theory/theory_inference_manager.cpp:564-568. Body: 'Node en = d_theoryState.getValuation().ensureLiteral(n); return d_out.preferPhase(en, pol);' -- it calls ensureLiteral first, so it is safe to call on a brand-new boolean skolem h that has no SAT literal yet.

Q1: OutputChannel::preferPhase(TNode n, bool phase) at src/theory/output_channel.h:109 (impl src/theory/output_channel.cpp:89-95 forwards to PropEngine::preferPhase). Its doc (output_channel.h:97-108) states the phase requirement is enforced GLOBALLY and context-INdependently: 'If you ever preferPhase() on a literal, it is phase-locked forever and ever', and n 'must have been pre-registered' with a SAT literal.

Q1: PropEngine::preferPhase(TNode n, bool phase) at src/prop/prop_engine.cpp:375-382 does 'SatLiteral lit = d_cnfStream->getLiteral(n); d_satSolver->preferPhase(phase ? lit : ~lit);' -- getLiteral fails if n was never CNF-ized, hence the ensureLiteral in TheoryInferenceManager::preferPhase. MinisatSatSolver::preferPhase (src/prop/minisat/minisat.cpp:276-283) implements it as d_minisat->freezePolarity(v, lit.isNegated()) -- a hard polarity freeze, not a soft preference.

Q1: Buffered alternative: InferenceManagerBuffered::addPendingPhaseRequirement(Node lit, bool pol) at src/theory/inference_manager_buffered.h:106 / .cpp:91-95, flushed by doPendingPhaseRequirements() (.cpp:130-138) which loops calling preferPhase. Doc (h:97-105): lit should have a SAT literal by the time doPendingPhaseRequirements is called, typically because it is a subformula of a pending lemma processed first. TheoryArith already does the right order: d_im.doPendingFacts(); d_im.doPendingLemmas(); d_im.doPendingPhaseRequirements(); at src/theory/arith/theory_arith.cpp:368-370 (inside needsCheckLastEffort).

Q2: arith's InferenceManager (src/theory/arith/inference_manager.h:40, extends InferenceManagerBuffered) declares three overloads (h:52-69, impl src/theory/arith/inference_manager.cpp:31-77): 'void addPendingLemma(std::unique_ptr<SimpleTheoryLemma> lemma, bool isWaiting = false)', 'void addPendingLemma(const SimpleTheoryLemma& lemma, bool isWaiting = false)', and 'void addPendingLemma(const Node& lemma, InferenceId inftype, ProofGenerator* pg = nullptr, bool isWaiting = false, LemmaProperty p = LemmaProperty::NONE)'. All return void; cached duplicates are silently dropped (cpp:36-39). These overloads HIDE the base-class bool-returning overload.

Q2: Base overloads: 'bool InferenceManagerBuffered::addPendingLemma(Node lem, InferenceId id, LemmaProperty p = LemmaProperty::NONE, ProofGenerator* pg = nullptr, bool checkCache = true)' at src/theory/inference_manager_buffered.h:64-68 / .cpp:49-67 (returns false if rewrite(lem) is already cached), and 'void addPendingLemma(std::unique_ptr<TheoryInference> lemma)' at h:73 / .cpp:69-73.

Q2: nullptr ProofGenerator while proof-producing is LEGAL and becomes a trusted THEORY_LEMMA step, not an assertion failure. Path: SimpleTheoryLemma::processLemma (src/theory/theory_inference.cpp:30-35) returns TrustNode::mkTrustLemma(d_node, d_pg) with d_pg possibly nullptr; TheoryInferenceManager::lemma does the same (theory_inference_manager.cpp:246-250); TheoryEngine::lemma (src/theory/theory_engine.cpp:1610, proof handling at 1641-1652) contains: 'if (isProofEnabled()) { if (tlemma.getGenerator() == nullptr) { Node tidn = builtin::BuiltinProofRuleChecker::mkTheoryIdNode(nodeManager(), from); d_lazyProof->addTrustedStep(lemma, TrustId::THEORY_LEMMA, {}, {tidn}); tlemma = TrustNode::mkTrustLemma(lemma, d_lazyProof.get()); } }'. The eager-check assertion 'Assert(tplemma.getGenerator() != nullptr)' in PropEngine::assertLemma (src/prop/prop_engine.cpp:195-198, only when proofCheck==EAGER) is satisfied because TheoryEngine already installed d_lazyProof as the generator.

Q3: Duplicate lemmas are dropped at TWO points. (a) Add time: arith::InferenceManager::addPendingLemma calls hasCachedLemma(lemma->d_node, lemma->d_property) and returns without queueing (src/theory/arith/inference_manager.cpp:36-39); InferenceManagerBuffered::addPendingLemma(Node,...) does the same when checkCache=true (src/theory/inference_manager_buffered.cpp:55-63). (b) Send time: doPendingLemmas (inference_manager_buffered.cpp:110-128) -> lemmaTheoryInference (cpp:161-169) -> TheoryInferenceManager::trustedLemma (src/theory/theory_inference_manager.cpp:252-275), which, when 'd_cacheLemmas && !isLemmaPropertyLocal(p)' (cpp:258), calls cacheLemma(tlem.getNode(), p) and returns false WITHOUT sending if the lemma is already cached (cpp:260-264).

Q3: The cache is d_lemmasSent, a user-context-dependent CDHashSet<Node> declared at src/theory/theory_inference_manager.h:476 and initialized d_lemmasSent(userContext()) at theory_inference_manager.cpp:45. cacheLemma (cpp:548-557) and hasCachedLemma (cpp:337-342) both operate on rewrite(lem) and IGNORE LemmaProperty. arith overrides hasCachedLemma/cacheLemma only to rewrite first and defer to base (src/theory/arith/inference_manager.cpp:100-110). Because the cache is user-context dependent, entries pop on user-context pop and the same lemma can be re-sent in a later user context. Because the cache is populated only at send time, two identical pending lemmas added in the same round both enter d_pendingLem; the second is dropped inside trustedLemma during doPendingLemmas.

Q3: hasSentLemma() (src/theory/theory_inference_manager.h:292, impl cpp:349-352) returns d_numCurrentLemmas != 0; d_numCurrentLemmas is incremented at cpp:272 only AFTER the cache check passes (so cache-dropped duplicates do not count) and is zeroed only by reset() (cpp:99-104). So hasSentLemma()/numSentLemmas() reflect lemmas actually emitted to the output channel since the last explicit reset() call by the theory -- not 'this round' automatically; TheoryArith must call d_im.reset() at the start of each round for the value to be per-round. Also note hasSent() (cpp:106-110) additionally includes conflicts and facts, and arith adds hasUsed() = hasSent() || hasPending() (arith/inference_manager.cpp:91).

Q4: LemmaProperty enum (src/theory/lemma_property.h:24-38): NONE=0, REMOVABLE=1, SEND_ATOMS=2, NEEDS_JUSTIFY=4, INPROCESS=8, LOCAL=16. There is NO 'PREPROCESS' property in this source tree; every lemma is unconditionally preprocessed via d_theoryProxy->preprocessLemma(tlemma, ppLemmas) in PropEngine::assertLemma (src/prop/prop_engine.cpp:192), which lifts term-level skolems/ITEs automatically, so liastar needs no special property for lemmas containing brand-new integer skolems y and boolean guard h.

Q4: SEND_ATOMS is consumed in OutputChannel::trustedLemma (src/theory/output_channel.cpp:139-142): 'if (isLemmaPropertySendAtoms(p)) { d_engine->ensureLemmaAtoms(plem.getNode(), d_theory); }' (ensureLemmaAtoms at src/theory/theory_engine.cpp:1501). It is only used by datatypes splits (theory_datatypes.cpp:1962) and arrays (theory_arrays.cpp:1416). It is NOT needed for new atoms to get SAT literals -- ordinary lemma CNF-ization preregisters all atoms in the lemma; SEND_ATOMS additionally pushes the atoms to the issuing theory as facts.

Q4: Properties liastar should AVOID on the guard lemmas h => base(y) and h => not(D_i(y)): REMOVABLE (PropEngine::assertLemma, prop_engine.cpp:186 -- the SAT solver may garbage-collect the clause, breaking the 'h forced false at decision level 0' completeness detection) and LOCAL (bypasses the lemma cache at theory_inference_manager.cpp:258 and is SAT-context-local / filtered via d_localLemmas in PropEngine::assertTrustedLemmaInternal, prop_engine.cpp:~226-243 -- lemma disappears on backtrack). Default LemmaProperty::NONE gives a persistent, user-context-scoped, cached lemma, which is what the enumeration scheme needs. NEEDS_JUSTIFY only matters when options().theory.relevanceFilter is on (src/theory/relevance_manager.cpp:546); INPROCESS permits inprocessing simplification of the clause (prop_engine.cpp:188) -- leave it unset so the h literal stays intact.
